redFlags: Seed contact details (phone 0300 065 3000, email enquiries@naturalresourceswales.gov.uk) are NRW's generic national Customer Hub, not site-specific — NRW's own page confirms 'there are no staff at this location'.

The visitor centre café and information desk were permanently CLOSED by NRW on 31 March 2025; only toilets remain plus the independently-run Beics Brenin bike shop/hire (which has its own separate phone number, 01341 440728, not affiliated to NRW's contact channel).
Site is an unstaffed, self-service forest park with paid parking (not free) — 'price Budget (parking only)' in the seed is directionally correct but parking is tiered/metered, not a flat small fee.

This is a government-run public amenity, not a bookable commercial operator: no claim/booking flow applies; content should read as a venue listing, and CTAs should point to the NRW parking/visitor page and Beics Brenin (for bike hire) rather than an enquiry form.

proposedOperatorData.name: Coed y Brenin Forest Park
proposedOperatorData.tagline: Britain's first purpose-built mountain bike centre, in a 9,000-acre Snowdonia forest
proposedOperatorData.description:
Coed y Brenin Forest Park, near Dolgellau, is a 9,000-acre Natural Resources Wales forest park in southern Snowdonia and the UK's first purpose-built mountain biking centre. It offers a graded network of MTB trails alongside gravel-bike routes, waymarked walking and running trails, orienteering, geocaching, and an off-road mobility-scooter route, set among waterfalls and mixed forest along the Afon Mawddach and Afon Wen.

The site is a Natural Resources Wales public amenity rather than a commercial tour operator: it is unstaffed, with no on-site NRW information desk or first aid provision. NRW's visitor centre café and information point permanently closed on 31 March 2025. Beics Brenin, an independent bike shop and hire centre, continues to operate on site daily (9am-5pm), and the trail network and toilets remain open and maintained.

Parking is paid and tiered (free for the first 30 minutes, rising to £12 for a full day), with an annual season ticket available; Blue Badge holders park free. As a public forest park there is no booking or claim process — visitors turn up and pay for parking on arrival, and bike hire is arranged separately and directly with Beics Brenin.
proposedOperatorData.uniqueSellingPoint: The original, most established purpose-built MTB trail centre in the UK, with a graded trail network for all abilities inside a working Snowdonia forest.
